prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the claims-triage agent (home and motor claims assessment within delegated authority) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: whether the home policy covers flooding. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 3)
response: {"items":[{"type":"fact","content":"When the policy wording says flood cover is included, check whether the water was external surface water, overflowing rivers or streams, or tidal ingress, treat it as a possible flood claim rather than assuming it is only storm damage."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the source of water is not obvious, ask for whether nearby land, roads, drains issue."},{"type":"fact","content":"When water enters after a blocked or overwhelmed drain outside the home, do not assume it is excluded, because many policies still regard that as flood if the cause
